name: libvisual-plugins
why: Audio visualisation plugins turn sound into shifting imagery, a classic transform, though the formula is just plugins and rather dated.

brief.what_it_is: Libvisual is a C/C++ audio visualisation library and framework, and the GitHub repository (Libvisual/libvisual) is its homepage. The README itself is short and only points to branches, build workflows and a wiki. The wiki says the project includes a command-line tool, lv-tool, for running visualisations. The README does not say what input the library takes or what output it produces. The Homebrew formula is named libvisual-plugins and is described as 'Audio Visualization tool and library', but the pages I read do not describe a separate plugin package, so I could not confirm what that formula installs.
brief.why_it_exists: The README gives no stated purpose. The wiki's news posts say the project exists to let applications use audio visualisations through a library API, and they describe its audience as both coders and application authors.
brief.how_it_works: The README does not explain the mechanism. The wiki news mentions a core library written in C++, a plugin-style set of visualisations, and a command-line runner, but I did not find a technical description of how audio is analysed or rendered.

commands_seen.context: From a 2013 wiki news post: the command-line tool for running visualisations, and the way to get its help output.

brief.install_notes: The README gives no installation steps beyond links to CI workflow files. For the 0.4.x branch (C99/C++11) the build uses GNU Autotools on Ubuntu/Debian. For the master branch, which targets 0.5.x (C11/C++20), the build uses CMake. There is also a Windows build check using mingw-w64 in CI. I did not check the Homebrew formula's dependencies or any runtime configuration.
brief.standout: The project is an old audio-visualisation library that has been revived, with a Windows CI build alongside Linux. Its wiki's news section records a long gap in development and a restart, which is unusual for a project that predates most current visualisers.
brief.status: quiet. The wiki's Project Status post dated 14 Jan 2023 says development has resumed after a long absence. Its release table lists 0.4.1 as released on 2022-12-06, while 0.4.2 and 0.5.0 are marked TBD. CI badges are present. I did not check the last commit date on the repository.
brief.caveats: The README is thin and the wiki's news is largely from 2013, so some of it may be out of date. Licence was not seen in the pages I read. The 0.4.x and 0.5.x branches use different language standards and build systems, so pick the branch deliberately. The Homebrew formula name and description refer to plugins, but the homepage I read covers the core library, and I could not confirm they match. The homepage is the core library repository, not a plugin package.
quotes: Development has resumed after another long absence!
Libvisual (LV) development is ongoing. Although the new API is in a state of flux, it is much more stable than master.
fetch_log: https://github.com/Libvisual/libvisual: worked; README returned, short, points to branches, build workflows and the wiki.
https://github.com/Libvisual/libvisual/wiki: worked; returned page text with navigation markup, including the Project Status news and release history.
